title.narrative: Pillar 1.2.3 [80 -10 -10] Strengthening access to integrated and inclusive Child Protection services to 2870 Refugees and 1111 Lebanese vulnerable children and caregivers in Hermel district.

description.narrative:
ltpgtlt/pgtltp class="MsoNormal" style="text-align:justify"gtltspan style="font-family:"gtIn line with the LCRP, ERP 2022 and the MOSA Strategic Plan 2020-27, the intervention mainly falls under Pillar I of the LHF allocation, since it puts at the center the protection needs of the most vulnerable children and their families and aims to address them through the delivery of inclusive and integrated CP services designed by adopting a holistic, integrated and community-based approach. In addition, the project guarantees cross-sectoral approach thanks to the synergies that will be created with the education projects implemented by TDH IT in the same areas through other funds (ECHO and AICS). lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtBuilding on existing projects, the initiative will take place in the vulnerable districts of Hermel areas. TDH IT will directly implement in ltagtHermel,lt/agtlt/spangtltspan class="MsoCommentReference" style="font-size: 14px"gtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif"gt lt/spangtlt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gt that is one of the most underserved areas, where TDHIT has a long-lasting presence and extended experience in the provision of CP services. Indirect implementation through Al Mabarrat local partner will be also covering Hermel areas. lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtThe intervention will address 3981 children and caregivers from Lebanese and Syrian refugees’ communities, supporting them with the provision of quality and inclusive CP prevention (Awareness, CBPSS, Caregivers Program) and response services (Focused PSS, Individual counselling and Case Management) tailored according to their specific needs, background and environment of living. Particular attention will be also given to the community engagement component through Social Behavioral Change and Communication activities (QUDWA initiatives), with a specific focus on increasing awareness on prevention mechanism for CP and SEA risks. lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtHigh quality inclusive CP intervention will be guaranteed through technical expertise, guidelines, and CP tools developed by TDH IT in partnership with UNICEF and following the guidance of the CP Working Group (CPWG). TDH IT and its partner will ensure compliance with the Minimum Standards of the CPWG as well as their internal standards of non-discrimination, transparency, and gender-sensitivity. As part of TDHITs integrated programming approach, children will benefit from a package of CP and education activities through a coordinated referral mechanism. lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtOutreach will be based on a comprehensive Area-Based approach following the Core Humanitarian Standards targeting vulnerable Persons of Concern (PoCs), while engaging with service providers, community/ religious leaders, and other stakeholders to mitigate the effects of instability in the society. A comprehensive vulnerability assessment will be rolled out to identify potential individuals through data generated on shelter conditions, access to healthcare, perceived safety and security of the area, and presence of HHs assets. Concurrently, the individual level data assesses individual vulnerabilities, aligned with the CP and EDU sectors (access/barriers to education, CP issues, employment status and child labor, trust networks) to identify vulnerable PoCs.lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="" style=""gtInclusion (Pillar 2) of children with disabilities (CwD) will be ensured from the assessment and outreach phases to the provision of services. TDHIT is currently co-leading the Inclusion Task Force with UNICEF and ensures that programs contribute to overcoming existing stigma and discrimination by removing barriers and guaranteeing equal opportunities to all children. In addition, TDHIT partner and other organizations will be trained on inclusive methodologies to actively involve CwDs and to mainstream inclusion. ltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtFinally, as part of its localization strategy (Pillar 3) and commitment to strengthening technical capacity of local partners, TDHIT will collaborate with national organizations operating in the CP sector, where partnerships are already in place. In particular, TDHIT will strengthen the capacity of the sub-IP, with a specific focus on Qudwa initiatives. The overall action will be evaluated through a robust outcome evaluation through multi-sectoral data and area-based analysis (Activity 2.2.3)lt/spangtlt/pgt
